title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (notation partly inferred). X is a smooth projective variety of dimension n, and S is a rational parameter variety; the arrangement of the diagram suggests S ≅ P^j. {Y_s} is a linear family of subvarieties of X. Its incidence cycle is Z ⊂ X × S, and C ⊂ X is the base locus, a smooth subvariety of codimension j+1.

Blow-up. Let f: X' → X be the blow-up of X along C ("éclaté"). Its exceptional divisor is α: P(N) → X', where N is the normal bundle of C. Because N is trivial here (C is cut out by j+1 members of the system), P(N) ≅ C × S. After blowing up, the family becomes a morphism X' → S.

Generic fibre. Let y be the generic point of S ("pt gén"). Then Y(y) is the generic member of the family, defined over k(S); i'_y: Y(y) → X' is the inclusion and i_y = f ∘ i'_y. The generic fibre of the exceptional divisor is C_y = C ⊗ k(S), with inclusion α_y: C_y → Y(y).

The argument.
1. Any cycle class y_y on Y(y) is the restriction of a class y' on X'; take the closure: y_y = i'_y^*(y').
2. Put x = f_*(y') ∈ A(X).
3. Blow-up formula: f^* f_* y' = y' + α_*(u), with u ∈ A(P(N)) = A(C × S).
4. Restricting to the generic fibre gives i_y^*(x) = i'_y^*(y') + i'_y^*(α_* u) = y_y + α_{y*}(u_y).
5. Since S is rational, A(C × S) is generated by A(C) ⊗ powers of the hyperplane class of S. Those powers restrict to 0 at the generic point, so u_y comes from A(C) ("Or u_y = u, u ∈ A(C)").

Conclusion (boxed): A(Y(y)) = Im A(X) + Im A(C). The graded version is A^i(Y(y)) = Im A^i(X) + Im A^{i-j}(C).

Purpose. This is a Lefschetz-type statement for Chow groups: algebraic cycles on the generic member of a linear system come from the ambient variety and from the base locus. It belongs to the cote's theme of the Hodge, Tate and Lefschetz conjectures, i.e. comparing cycles on hyperplane or linear sections with cycles on the ambient variety. The previous page (EGA-style dévissage) and the next page (sketches of nodal curves) are unrelated.
errors: Codimension bookkeeping in the graded formula is doubtful. If P(N) ≅ C × S and C has codimension j+1, then S ≅ P^j and the fibres Y(y) have dimension n−j. C_y then has dimension n−j−1, i.e. it is a divisor in Y(y), so push-forward should shift degree by 1: A^i(Y(y)) = Im A^i(X) + Im A^{i-1}(C). The written A^{i-j}(C) agrees with this only for j = 1 (a pencil). The label 'codim j' beside α_y is likewise inconsistent unless it refers to the codimension of Y(y) in X.

'u_y = u, u ∈ A(C)' is shorthand. In fact u ∈ A(C × S), and one needs that S is rational, so that A(C × P^j) = ⊕ A(C)·h^k and h restricts to 0 at the generic point. This is presumably why 'variété rationnelle' is noted.

Implicit hypotheses: X and C smooth (needed for f^* and for the blow-up formula). Also implicit: the surjectivity A(X') → A(Y(y)), by taking closures of cycles on the generic fibre. In 'i'_y^*(y') = y'' the result should be denoted y_y.

ideas.what: Chow groups of the generic member of a linear system with base locus C are generated by restriction from X plus push-forward from C, proved via blow-up of the base locus and the key formula f^*f_*y' = y' + α_*(u).
ideas.modern_name: Chow groups of the generic hyperplane / linear section (generic-fibre spreading argument); blow-up formula for Chow groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. The blow-up formula is in Manin (1968) and Fulton (Intersection Theory, Prop. 6.7). Generic-section arguments of this kind appear in Bloch–Srinivas-style spreading and in Voisin's work on Chow groups of generic hypersurfaces.
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such. The Lefschetz-type context matches 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), but this computation does not appear there.

ideas.what: Using rationality of the parameter space so that cycles on C × S restrict at the generic point to cycles coming from C.
ideas.modern_name: Projective bundle formula / restriction to the generic point (CH(C_{k(S)}) is a quotient of CH(C × S))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Grothendieck's projective bundle formula, 1958 'La théorie des classes de Chern')
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'La théorie des classes de Chern' (1958); SGA 6

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct-in-spirit sketch of a standard Lefschetz-type statement for Chow groups of the generic member of a linear system with base locus. It is folklore today, and the only notable feature is the small codimension slip in the graded version.
transcription_corrections: 'Z^i(Y' is probably 'Z^i(Y)' (cycles of codimension i on Y).
'y_y = i_y'^*(y')': the left side is the given cycle on Y(y), y_y.
In '= y' + α_{y*}(u_y)' the first term should be y_y (Grothendieck's abuse of notation).
'G^{al}[?]' at the bottom is likely an abbreviation such as 'Gal' / 'En gal' (= en général) introducing the graded version, rather than a Galois symbol.
'C × S ≀ P(N)': the ≀ is a vertical isomorphism sign, P(N) ≅ C × S.
